files.migration_notes:
Replace jQuery CDN script with React entry point. Add a root div (e.g.,
) for React to mount. Change script tag to type="module" and point to /src/main.jsx. Remove the inline script reference to app.js. Keep the same HTML structure for the task board UI but ensure all id/class attributes match what the React component will expect (they can remain identical). Update the title and meta tags as needed for a React/Vite project.

CSS is largely compatible with React. No changes required for selectors or rules. However, note that in JSX we use className instead of class, but the CSS file itself remains unchanged. Import this file in src/main.jsx with `import './App.css'`. Ensure the file is placed in src/ so the import works. The existing styles for .completed, .task-text, .delete-btn, etc., will apply directly to the React-rendered elements.

Convert the entire jQuery logic into a single React functional component (TaskBoard) and render it into the root div. Key conversions:
- Replace $(document).ready with component initialization (useState, useEffect).
- State: showingCompletedOnly -> useState(false); tasks array -> useState([]) loaded from API.
- updateStats: compute from tasks state (total, completed, remaining) and render in JSX.
- appendTask: replace with adding a task object to tasks state (id, title, completed).
- Event handlers: onClick for add, delete, toggle, clear; onChange for checkbox. Use synthetic events.
- AJAX: use useEffect with fetch to load initial tasks from 'https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/todos?_limit=3' and set tasks state.
- DOM manipulation (show/hide, toggleClass, append/remove) replaced by conditional rendering and state updates.
- li.data('taskId') replaced by task.id in state objects.
- Render task list by mapping tasks state to <li> elements with checkbox, span, button.
- Import './App.css' at top of file.
- Export default TaskBoard and render with ReactDOM.createRoot(root).render(<TaskBoard />).
- Ensure all class attributes become className in JSX.

IMPORTANT: The migrated stylesheet is already imported globally by the app's entry point (main.jsx). Do NOT add any CSS import statement to this file yourself, and do not reference any CSS filename directly in this file.

OVERRIDE — IGNORE ANY CONFLICTING INSTRUCTION ABOVE: Do NOT call createRoot, ReactDOM.render, or any app-mounting code anywhere in this file, even if an earlier note in this same message said to. This file must ONLY define the component and end with `export default ComponentName;` — nothing else. The actual mounting is handled entirely by a separate entry point file (main.jsx) that is not part of this migration and already exists.

overall_notes: Migration strategy: Convert the monolithic jQuery script into a single React component (TaskBoard) within src/main.jsx, keeping the HTML template (index.html) and styles (src/App.css) as separate files. This respects the one-to-one file mapping constraint. Risks: The original code mixes data fetching, DOM manipulation, and UI logic tightly; the React version must separate concerns via state and effects. The AJAX call uses a placeholder API; ensure CORS allows fetch from the development server. The toggle-completed filter logic must be reimplemented as a derived view (filter tasks state) rather than DOM show/hide. Testing should verify that adding, completing, deleting, and filtering tasks work identically. Use Vite for development (as per reference) with environment variable prefix VITE_ if needed later.
